main_text.p: liter & cives. Prævaluerunt tamen Dominicani Papæ devoti, ob multimoda eorum obsequia.

Matthæus Parisius: Anno Domini 1256. crescentibus bescentibus[?] scandalis & odiis inter magistros Parisienses & fratres Prædicatores, seu Dominicanos, electi sunt cum magna deliberatione, celeberrimi magistri, Guilhelmus de S. Amore, Odo vel Otho de Doaco, Christianum canonicum Belvacensis, Nicolaum Barum super Albam, Ioannes Driton vel de Sicca villa Anglicum, rector universitatis Parisiensis; & Ioannes Belin Gallicum, omnes philosophi, omnes rectores in artibus, in decretis, & in theologia, ex nobilibus procreati, ut Romam adirent ad Dominum Papam, pro tranquillitate universitatis Parisiensis ac fidei redintegratione, quæ detrimentum patiebatur magnum. Nam fratres nova quaedam prædicabant, legebant & docebant deliramenta, ex libris Ioachim abbatis. Incipit eorum liber, Evangelium æternum: & quædam alia, quæ non expedit recitari. Prædicatores autem suos ex expeditos nuncios contra universitatem miserunt, ut magistris in faciem contradicerent. Subsannabat populus, eleemosynas consuetas subtrahendo: vocans eos hypocritas, Antichristi successores, pseudo-prædicatores, regum deceptores, principum adulatores, falsos cōfiliarios, ordinariorum cōtemptores, &

page.notes: The line "nova quaedam" is underlined in the print, as are the words "Dominicanos" and "Nam fratres nova quaedam" in the Latin lines; underlining is not marked. Doubtful: the word after "crescentibus" (first letter, read as b) and "in faciem" (the long s/f form is unclear). "Expeditos" is joined from "ex / peditos" with no printed hyphen. Two mid-line word breaks ("celeber-rimi", "delira-menta") show no printed hyphen and are written whole. The final "&" stands alone at the foot and is taken as the last word of the paragraph, not as a catchword.
